places.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Bukchon Hanok Village
places.nearest_station: Gyeongbokgung Station (Subway Line 3, Exit 5) or Anguk Station (Line 3, Exit 3)
places.autumn_highlight: The ginkgo trees along the stone palace walls turn vibrant golden yellow in early November. Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00 daily (closed Tuesdays).

places.name: Myeongdong Shopping Street & N Seoul Tower
places.autumn_highlight: Take the Namsan Suncheon Circular Green Bus #01 up to N Seoul Tower for 360-degree sunset views of Seoul's autumn foliage.

places.name: Hongdae Youth Culture & Gyeongui Line Forest Park
places.nearest_station: Hongik University Station (Subway Line 2, AREX, Gyeongui-Jungang Line)
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 15 min from Seoul Station via AREX All-Stop
places.autumn_highlight: Yeonnam-dong's Gyeongui Line Forest Park (Yeontral Park) is lined with orange maple trees and cozy autumn terrace cafes.

places.name: Gangnam District & COEX Starfield Library
places.nearest_station: Samseong Station (Subway Line 2) or Bongeunsa Station (Subway Line 9)
places.autumn_highlight: Across from COEX Mall is Bongeunsa Temple, a 1,200-year-old Buddhist sanctuary where red maples frame skyscrapers.

places.name: Seongsu-dong ('The Brooklyn of Seoul') & DDP
places.nearest_station: Seongsu Station (Subway Line 2) / Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station (Line 2/4/5)
places.autumn_highlight: Industrial brick warehouses converted into flagship fashion pop-ups and artisan bakeries, surrounded by autumn street trees.

places.name: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (UNESCO Day Trip)
places.nearest_station: Suwon Station (KORAIL ITX-Saemaeul / KTX / Subway Line 1)
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 30 min via ITX-Saemaeul Train from Seoul Station (or 60 min via Subway Line 1)
places.autumn_highlight: Walk the 5.7 km 18th-century stone fortress walls surrounded by red ginkgos and silver grass. Stunning archery pavilion views.

places.name: Nami Island & Gapyeong Autumn Foliage
places.transit_card_used: KORAIL ITX-Cheongchun Ticket (Book on KorailTalk app)
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 50 min from Yongsan Station or Cheongnyangni Station
places.autumn_highlight: Korea's most famous autumn destination! Walk the Ginkgo Tree Lane and Metasequoia Lane under a golden canopy.

places.name: DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) & Imjingak Peace Park
places.nearest_station: Imjingak Station (DMZ Peace Train / Verified Tourist Shuttle)
places.autumn_highlight: Visit the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel and Dora Observatory overlooking North Korea. Civilian access requires passport and booking.

places.name: Seoraksan National Park & Sokcho Coastal Village
places.transit_card_used: Express Bus Ticket (Book via KOBUS / T-money GO)
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 2 hr 20 min via Express Bus from Seoul Express Bus Terminal (Gangnam)
places.autumn_highlight: The premier granite mountain range of South Korea. Take the Seoraksan Cable Car up to Gwongeumseong Fortress for crimson foliage peaks.

places.name: Haeundae Beach & Blue Line Park Coastal Train
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 45 min from Busan KTX Station via Metro
places.autumn_highlight: Crisp ocean breezes, golden beach sunsets, and the retro Haeundae Beach Train running along coastal cliffs from Mipo to Songjeong.

places.name: Gamcheon Culture Village & Jagalchi Seafood Market
places.nearest_station: Toseong Station (Busan Metro Line 1, Exit 6) + Town Bus Saha 1-1 / 2-2
places.autumn_highlight: The 'Machu Picchu of Busan' features colorful terraced houses overlooking the ocean. Walk down to Jagalchi Market for fresh autumn seafood.

places.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Seaside Temple
places.nearest_station: Osiria Station (Dong해 Line) or Bus #181 / Kakao T Taxi from Haeundae
places.autumn_highlight: One of the only Buddhist temples in Korea built directly on ocean rocks, dramatic wave crashes under crisp November skies.

places.name: Gyeongju Historic Center (Option A - Top Recommended)
places.nearest_station: Singyeongju Station (KTX / SRT) -> Bus #700 into Historic Center
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 35 min KTX from Busan Station (or 2 hr 05 min KTX from Seoul Station)
places.autumn_highlight: Bulguksa Temple, Seokguram Grotto, and Daereungwon Tumuli Park offer the most magnificent crimson maple and golden ginkgo displays in South Korea.

places.name: Jeju Island (Option B - Volcanic Island)
places.transit_card_used: Domestic Flight + Tourist Taxi Charter / T-money
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 1 hr flight from Busan Gimhae (PUS) or Seoul Gimpo (GMP)
places.autumn_highlight: Silver grass waving across volcanic oreums and Hallasan National Park trails.

places.name: Jeonju Hanok Heritage Village (Option C - Food Capital)
places.nearest_station: Jeonju Station (KTX) -> 15 min Kakao T Taxi
places.est_transit_time_from_center: 1 hr 40 min KTX from Seoul Yongsan Station
places.autumn_highlight: Over 800 traditional wooden Hanok houses surrounded by ancient ginkgo trees at Jeonju Hyanggyo Confucian School.

routes.recommendation: Reserved seating, dedicated luggage racks, free Wi-Fi. Easiest and fastest non-stop ride to central Seoul.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Direct equivalent to Tokyo's Narita Express (N'EX) or Skyliner.

routes.recommendation: Stops at Hongik Univ. (Hongdae) and Gongdeok. Cheaper than express, but commuter subway style seating (no reserved seats). Pay with T-money or WOWPASS.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like BART from SFO to downtown SF or Tokyo's Keisei Main Line.

routes.recommendation: No stairs or subway transfers! Driver loads your heavy bags underneath and drops you directly in front of major hotels.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Direct equivalent to Japan's Airport Limousine Bus from Narita/Haneda to Shinjuku hotels.

routes.mode: Official Airport Taxi / Kakao T / Uber
routes.recommendation: Total metered cost is ~60,000 to 70,000 KRW including highway toll. Split between 2 travelers ($23/person), it is extremely convenient if you have heavy luggage after a transpacific flight.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Way cheaper than taking an Uber from SFO to Marin or Tokyo Narita taxi ($200+).

routes.recommendation: Best overall balance of speed, comfort, and center-to-center convenience. If traveling round-trip or connecting to a 3rd city, check the KORAIL Saver Pass (for 2-5 travelers) to save up to 40,000+ KRW.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Similar to riding the Tokaido Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto, but ~50% cheaper.

routes.iphone_app: SRT (Korean only - book via website in English)
routes.recommendation: About 10% cheaper than KTX and departs from Gangnam (Suseo). Highly recommended if your hotel is in southern Seoul, though tickets sell out very quickly.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like an alternative Shinkansen line departing from a southern hub station.

routes.recommendation: Feature 160-degree flat reclining individual pods with privacy curtains and personal entertainment screens. Best budget option with luxury comfort.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Far more luxurious than greyhound/California buses; comparable to Japan's premium highway luxury coaches.

routes.mode: Domestic Flight (Korean Air, Asiana, Air Busan, Jeju Air)
routes.duration: 1 hr flight (approx 3 hr 30 min total door-to-door)
routes.recommendation: Flight time is only 60 mins, but add airport transit and security time. Good if you find a sale (~35,000 KRW one-way), but KTX is more relaxing and drops you in central Busan.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like flying SFO to LAX on a short shuttle flight.

routes.recommendation: The fastest way to reach historic Gyeongju (Option A for 3rd City). From Singyeongju Station, take Bus 700 or a 15-minute taxi into the historic UNESCO center.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like taking the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Kyoto's historic temple districts.

routes.recommendation: Lightning-fast 35-minute hop! Makes Busan <-> Gyeongju an effortless combination on your itinerary.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Shorter and faster than BART from downtown SF to SFO.

routes.frequency: World's busiest air route (flights every 5-10 minutes)
routes.recommendation: Essential mode if you select Jeju Island as your 3rd city. Book early for peak autumn foliage weekends in November.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like flying from Tokyo to Okinawa or SFO to Honolulu, but with 10x flight frequency.

routes.recommendation: The culinary capital of Korea (Option C for 3rd City). Quick 1 hour 40 min train from Yongsan Station in Seoul.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like taking an express train from Tokyo to a historic gourmet town like Kanazawa.

routes.recommendation: Reserved comfortable seats! Much faster and more relaxing than taking the All-Stop Subway Line 1 (which takes 60 mins).
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like taking a JR Limited Express train from Tokyo to Kamakura.

routes.recommendation: Korea's only double-decker express train! Drops you at Gapyeong Station where you take a 5-minute taxi or bus to the Nami Island ferry.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like the double-decker Green Car on JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line.

routes.to: Sokcho Express Bus Terminal (Seoraksan National Park)
routes.recommendation: The most comfortable way to reach Seoraksan National Park for dramatic November mountain foliage.
routes.sf_japan_comparison: Like taking a highway coach from Tokyo to Hakone or Fuji Five Lakes.

apps.name: Naver Map, Navigation
apps.why_essential: Google Maps walking and driving directions do not work in South Korea due to national security and mapping laws. Naver Map is the #1 gold standard for precise subway platforms, bus arrival countdowns, and walking paths.
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Your replacement for Google Maps and Apple Maps in Korea.
apps.beginner_tip: In App Settings -> Language, switch to English. You can save favorite places (like your hotel) in custom lists. It shows exact exit numbers for subway stations!

apps.name: KakaoMap - Korea No.1 Map
apps.why_essential: Great backup/alternative to Naver Map. Many locals prefer KakaoMap for bus arrival accuracy and street-view ('Road View') quality.
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Like Citymapper for Seoul and Busan.
apps.beginner_tip: Works seamlessly with Kakao T when calling a taxi to a specific pin on the map.

apps.name: Kakao T (Taxi, Bike, Driver)
apps.why_essential: The undisputed king of taxi dispatching in South Korea. Never worry about language barriers with taxi drivers—your destination is sent automatically to the driver's GPS.
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Direct equivalent to Uber or Lyft in San Francisco, or JapanTaxi/GO app in Tokyo.
apps.beginner_tip: You can use Kakao T without a Korean credit card! Select 'General Taxi' and choose 'Pay to Driver' (Cash/Card to driver) as your payment method. Pay the driver with your WOWPASS, T-money, or foreign Visa/Mastercard at the end of the ride.

apps.name: Uber / UT
apps.why_essential: In South Korea, the global Uber app operates as a joint venture called UT, dispatching official licensed taxis. If you already have Uber installed on your iPhone from SF, it works right away!
apps.sf_japan_comparison: The exact same Uber app you use in San Francisco—your saved credit card in Uber will be charged automatically in KRW.
apps.beginner_tip: Compare prices between Kakao T and Uber during rush hours. Uber often has promos for first-time rides in Korea.

apps.name: KorailTalk
apps.why_essential: The official KORAIL app for booking KTX high-speed trains between Seoul, Busan, Gyeongju, and Jeonju.
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Like the SmartEX app for Japan Shinkansen or Amtrak app.
apps.beginner_tip: Set language to English in the top-right menu. Book KTX tickets 2-4 weeks in advance for weekend travel (tickets open 1 month in advance at 07:00 KST).

apps.name: Subway Korea (Malang Studio)
apps.why_essential: The fastest, most reliable English subway map and timetable app for Seoul, Busan, Daegu, Gwangju, and Daejeon. Works offline!
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Like Japan Travel by NAVITIME subway view or BART official app.
apps.beginner_tip: Shows which subway car door (e.g. Car 4, Door 2) to board for the fastest transfer or exit!

apps.name: Naver Papago - AI Translator
apps.why_essential: Naver's AI translation engine is vastly superior to Google Translate for Korean honorifics, idioms, and natural grammar. Essential for dining, taxis, and shopping.
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Far more accurate for Korean than Google Translate.
apps.beginner_tip: Use 'Image Translation' mode to snap photos of Korean restaurant menus or bus terminal signs for instant English overlays!

apps.name: T-money GO (Integrated Transit & Express Bus)
apps.why_essential: Book highway express buses and intercity buses nationwide. Also integrates city bike rentals (Ttareungyi in Seoul).
apps.sf_japan_comparison: Like a Greyhound/Flixbus app combined with city bikeshare.
apps.beginner_tip: If you have trouble with international credit cards on the app, you can check bus schedules here and buy tickets at the terminal ticket machines or windows.

apps.name: BUSTAGO (Intercity Bus Reservation)
apps.why_essential: Official nationwide intercity bus booking platform. Essential for routes to smaller towns or direct airport bus connections.
apps.beginner_tip: Supports English interface and ticket QR codes.

cards.name: T-money Transit Card
cards.where_to_buy: All convenience stores (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven, Emart24) and subway station ticket machines.
cards.where_to_recharge: Convenience stores or subway station machines (CASH ONLY in KRW for standard T-money).
cards.coverage: Subways, buses, taxis, and convenience stores nationwide across all of South Korea (Seoul, Busan, Gyeongju, Jeju, Jeonju).
cards.best_for: Every traveler! This is the mandatory baseline card in Korea.
cards.sf_japan_equivalent: Direct equivalent to SF Clipper Card or Japan Suica / Pasmo / ICOCA.
cards.pro_tip: Always tap ON when boarding and tap OFF when exiting buses and subways to get free/discounted transfers within 30 minutes!

cards.name: WOWPASS (All-in-One Tourist Prepaid Debit + T-money)
cards.type: All-in-One Foreigner Payment Card + Transit Card
cards.where_to_buy: WOWPASS Kiosks at Incheon Airport, Seoul Station, major subway stations, and hotels.
cards.where_to_recharge: Insert USD/EUR/JPY/GBP cash into kiosk to top up KRW debit balance; top up T-money transit balance at convenience stores or subway machines.
cards.coverage: Accepted as a regular IC debit card at 99% of shops, cafes, restaurants in Korea + built-in T-money IC chip for subways/buses.
cards.best_for: First-time foreign tourists who want to avoid carrying stacks of KRW cash while getting competitive exchange rates.
cards.sf_japan_equivalent: Like a Suica card combined with an international tourist debit card.
cards.pro_tip: Download the official WOWPASS iPhone app to track your expenses in real-time, lock the card if lost, and get cashback at olive young / Starbucks.

cards.name: Seoul Climate Card (Tourist Short-Term Pass - 2026)
cards.type: Unlimited Transit Pass for Seoul Subways & Buses
cards.where_to_buy: Seoul Subway station Customer Safety Centers (Lines 1-8) and convenience stores near tourist hubs.
cards.where_to_recharge: Valid for 1, 2, 3, 5, or 7 consecutive days (e.g., 5-Day Pass is only 15,000 KRW = ~$10.70 USD!).
cards.coverage: Unlimited rides on Seoul subways and Seoul city buses (blue, green, yellow). Excludes AREX Express, Shinbundang line, and intercity buses outside Seoul.
cards.best_for: Travelers spending 3 to 7 intensive days exploring Seoul and riding transit 3+ times per day.
cards.sf_japan_equivalent: Like the Tokyo Subway 72-hour Ticket or SF Muni 3-Day Visitor Passport, but insanely cheap.
cards.pro_tip: At 15,000 KRW for 5 days, you break even after just 10 subway rides! A massive money saver for your Seoul days.

cards.name: KORAIL Saver Pass (for Groups of 2 to 5 Travelers)
cards.type: Unlimited KTX & Korail Train Tourist Pass
cards.where_to_buy: Official KORAIL website or verified partners (Klook, Trazy).
cards.where_to_recharge: 2-Day Flexible (121,000 KRW/person) or 4-Day Flexible (224,000 KRW/person) for 2+ travelers.
cards.coverage: Unlimited KTX, ITX, and Mugunghwa train rides nationwide (excludes SRT). Includes up to 2 free seat reservations per day.
cards.best_for: Two travelers doing multi-city trips like Seoul -> Busan -> Gyeongju/Jeonju -> Seoul.
cards.sf_japan_equivalent: Direct equivalent to the Japan Rail (JR) Pass, but specifically discounted for groups of 2-5 people!
cards.pro_tip: If you buy individual roundtrip KTX tickets Seoul-Busan it costs ~119,600 KRW. The 2-Day Flexible Saver Pass is 121,000 KRW and lets you add additional intercity KTX legs for virtually zero extra cost!

cards.name: Discover Seoul Pass (DSP)
cards.type: Attractions + AREX Express Train + T-money Function
cards.where_to_buy: Official website, Incheon Airport kiosks, or Klook.
cards.coverage: Free entry to 70+ top attractions (Lotte World, N Seoul Tower, Gyeongbokgung Palace) + 1 free AREX Express train ticket + T-money card.
cards.best_for: First-time visitors who want to pack major tourist sights and airport transport into 48-72 hours.
cards.sf_japan_equivalent: Like the San Francisco CityPASS or Osaka Amazing Pass.
cards.pro_tip: Use the physical card as a permanent T-money transit card even after your 24/48/72h attraction window expires!

cards.name: Visit Busan Pass
cards.where_to_buy: Visit Busan Pass website, Busan Station, or Klook.
cards.where_to_recharge: 24h Pass (55,000 KRW), 48h Pass (85,000 KRW), or Big3/Big5 Flex Pass.
cards.coverage: Free entry to Haeundae Blue Line Park Beach Train, Busan X the Sky, Lotte World Busan, Skyline Luge + built-in transit card.
cards.best_for: 2-3 days of coastal sightseeing in Busan.
cards.sf_japan_equivalent: Direct equivalent to Osaka Amazing Pass for Busan.
cards.pro_tip: The Haeundae Beach Train and Busan X the Sky observation deck alone cover more than 70% of the 24h pass price!

stations.name: Seoul Station (KTX / AREX / Subway Lines 1 & 4)
stations.arex_express_location: B2 - B7 (Underground Airport Railroad concourse). Follow orange 'Airport Railroad Express' signs.
stations.wowpass_tmoney_location: WOWPASS Kiosks located near AREX gates (B2) and Subway Line 1 concourse. T-money recharge at any subway ticket machine (cash only).

luggage_services.name: T-Luggage (Seoul Metro Official)
luggage_services.location: Underground passage between Exit 1 and Exit 2
luggage_services.cost: 9,000 KRW for 4 hrs (weekdays) / 13,000 KRW (weekends), +1,000 KRW/hr after
luggage_services.notes: Face-to-face counter, offers same-day hotel and airport luggage delivery.

luggage_services.name: Zimcarry (KORAIL KTX Official)
luggage_services.location: Main KTX concourse near 2nd floor shopping area
luggage_services.cost: 10,000 KRW for 4 hrs, or ~15,000-20,000 KRW for same-day delivery to Busan/hotel
luggage_services.notes: Best service for forwarding heavy bags from Seoul Station directly to your Busan hotel!

luggage_services.name: T-Locker / LuggageQ (24/7 Coin Lockers)
luggage_services.location: Near Exit 15 and throughout B1 subway interchange
luggage_services.cost: ~1,000 KRW per hour per locker (one locker fits 2-3 large 27-inch suitcases)
luggage_services.notes: Self-service touchscreen kiosks with English interface. Pay by credit card or T-money.

stations.transfer_tip: When transferring from Subway Line 1 or 4 to KTX, allow at least 10-15 minutes to navigate the escalator concourses.

stations.name: Busan KTX Station & Busan Metro Line 1
stations.arex_express_location: N/A (Use Gimhae Light Rail or Airport Limousine Bus for Gimhae Airport)
stations.wowpass_tmoney_location: WOWPASS Kiosk inside 2nd floor KTX waiting hall. T-money/Busan Metro machines on B1.

luggage_services.name: Zimcarry Busan Station Desk
luggage_services.location: 2nd floor KTX waiting hall near Exit 1
luggage_services.cost: ~15,000 KRW per large suitcase for hotel delivery or airport transfer
luggage_services.notes: Drop your suitcases when your KTX arrives at 11:30 AM and go straight to Haeundae Beach empty-handed! Bags arrive at your hotel by 4 PM.

stations.transfer_tip: Exit 1 on the 2nd floor leads to the pedestrian deck and Busan Metro Line 1 (Orange Line) entrance.

stations.name: Singyeongju Station (Gyeongju KTX / SRT)
stations.category: High-Speed Rail Gateway to Historic Gyeongju
stations.wowpass_tmoney_location: Convenience store (StoryWay / CU) inside station hall.

luggage_services.name: Singyeongju Station Luggage Lockers
luggage_services.location: Main waiting hall to the right of the exit gates
luggage_services.notes: Coin/card lockers. Ideal if you want to explore Bulguksa Temple before checking into your hotel.

stations.transfer_tip: Exit 1 leads directly to the bus terminal for Bus #700 and the official Kakao T taxi stand.

stations.name: Incheon International Airport (ICN - T1 / T2)
stations.arex_express_location: Transportation Center (B1) in both Terminal 1 and Terminal 2.
stations.wowpass_tmoney_location: WOWPASS Kiosks located in Arrivals Hall (1F) and AREX ticket area (B1). CU/GS25 convenience stores sell T-money cards.

luggage_services.name: Hanjin Express / Airport Baggage Delivery
luggage_services.location: Terminal 1 (3F near check-in counter B/N) and Terminal 2 (1F/3F)
luggage_services.cost: ~15,000 - 25,000 KRW per suitcase for same-day hotel delivery in Seoul
luggage_services.notes: Drop bags after landing and ride AREX to Seoul empty-handed.

stations.transfer_tip: If flying Korean Air or Asiana on Day 23 departure, use the Seoul Station City Airport Terminal (B2) to check your luggage and clear immigration downtown before boarding AREX!

stationExits.avoid_exit: Exit 3 / Exit 4 (Long steep stairs with no elevator)
stationExits.nearby_hub: Myeongdong Shopping Street & Namsan Bus #01 Stop
Yeonnam-dong Gyeongui Line Forest Park & AREX All-Stop Terminal

stationExits.best_luggage_exit: Exit 15 (Elevator to KTX Concourse) or Underground Exit 1-2 (T-Luggage)
stationExits.nearby_hub: KTX High-Speed Rail Concourse & AREX Express Gate B2

stationExits.best_luggage_exit: KTX Exit 1 (Pedestrian Deck Elevator to Metro Line 1)
stationExits.nearby_hub: Zimcarry Luggage Desk & Express Bus #1003 to Haeundae

contingencies.plan_b: The Hyundai Seoul (Yeouido) Indoor Botanical Mall & National Museum of Korea
contingencies.transit_mode: Subway Line 5 (Yeouinaru Station) / Line 4 (Ichon Underground Walkway)
contingencies.why_better: Both venues are connected directly to subway exits via covered underground tunnels—zero rain exposure!

contingencies.plan_b: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress or Eunpyeong Hanok Village
contingencies.transit_mode: ITX-Saemaeul Train (30 min) or Subway Line 3 + Bus #7211
contingencies.why_better: Nami Island ferry lines on November weekends can exceed 45 minutes. Suwon's 5.7 km fortress wall never feels crowded.

contingencies.plan_a: Taejongdae Cliff Walking & Songdo Cable Car
contingencies.plan_b: Spa Land Centum City (Luxury Korean Sauna) & Shinsegae Mall + Busan X the Sky
contingencies.transit_mode: Busan Metro Line 2 (Centum City Station - Underground direct entrance)
contingencies.why_better: Spa Land is an 18-temperature therapeutic hot spring sauna inside the world's largest department store.

contingencies.plan_b: Gyeongju National Museum & Hwangnyongwon Tea Pavilion
contingencies.transit_mode: Kakao T Taxi (~6,000 KRW) or Bus #10 / #11
contingencies.why_better: World-class Silla gold crowns and artifacts indoors.

bikeShare.how_to_use: Rent directly inside the T-money GO iPhone app using your international credit card or WOWPASS without Korean resident registration.
bikeShare.cost: 1,000 KRW (~$0.70 USD) for 1 hour of cycling
bikeShare.best_route: Yeouido Han River Park loop to Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain.

bikeShare.how_to_use: Rent bikes outside Singyeongju Station or along Hwangridan-gil.
bikeShare.best_route: Flat cycling path from Daereungwon Burial Mounds to Cheomseongdae Observatory and Wolji Pond.

rules: Immediate Tax Refund (즉시 환급) is available at Olive Young, Lotte Mart, Uniqlo, and major department stores for purchases between 15,000 KRW and 1,000,000 KRW.
Always carry your physical passport or e-passport scan to the cashier.
If spend exceeds 1,000,000 KRW, obtain an Airport Tax Refund receipt and scan it at the Incheon Airport T1/T2 automated kiosks before security check-in.

transitFood.spot_name: Korail Dosirak (`도시락` - Train Bento) & Kakao Friends Cafe
transitFood.best_item: Bulgogi & Kimchi Hanwoo Bento Box (11,000 KRW / ~$7.80 USD)
transitFood.tip: Buy your bento box 15 minutes before your KTX departs and eat at your seat!

transitFood.spot_name: Samjin Amook (`삼진어묵` - Busan Gourmet Fish Cake Bakery)
transitFood.best_item: Cheese Amook Croquette & Hot Fish Cake Skewer (3,500 KRW / ~$2.50 USD)
transitFood.tip: Busan's most iconic snack bakery is located right inside the KTX waiting hall.

transitFood.hub: Express Bus Highway Rest Area (`휴게소` - Hyugeso)
transitFood.best_item: Sotteok Sotteok (`소떡소떡` - Sausage & Rice Cake Skewer) + Walnut Pastry (`호두과자` - Hodu-gwaja)
transitFood.tip: On your Premium Gold bus ride, the driver will pause for 15 minutes at a highway rest area. Remember your bus license plate number!

logistics.logistics_philosophy: We prioritize 'The Korea Transit Sweet Spot': finding the lowest cost transportation that does NOT sacrifice convenience, time, or hassle. Saving $4 on an airport train after a 12-hour flight or saving $14 on an intercity bus to sit in 2 hours of highway traffic is a poor trade-off.

cheapest_option.hassle_level: High (Subway bench seats, crowded with commuters, standing with heavy luggage)

sweet_spot_option.hassle_level: Zero (Reserved reclining seats, dedicated luggage racks, free Wi-Fi, drops at Seoul Station)
sweet_spot_option.why_sweet_spot: For only $9.35 extra total for both travelers, you eliminate commuter crowds and get a relaxing non-stop express ride after a transpacific flight.

hotelTripTemplate.title: South Korea Trip — Seoul · Gyeongju · Busan
hotelTripTemplate.note: Oct 31 – Nov 22, 2026 (22 nights). Autumn shoulder season — leaf-peeping, mild temps, lighter crowds than summer, and generally better hotel rates than spring high season. Prices below are typical nightly USD figures for a standard double; always confirm the live rate for YOUR dates on the hotel's official site.

hotelSplitTemplate.recommended: Seoul 8 nights (Oct 31–Nov 8) · Gyeongju 6 nights (Nov 8–Nov 14) · Busan 8 nights (Nov 14–Nov 22)
hotelSplitTemplate.rationale: Seoul is the biggest city and main transport hub, so bookending the trip there is practical. Gyeongju is compact (5–7 nights = relaxed pace + day trips to Bulguksa & Yangdong Village). Busan is large and spread across two personalities (Haeundae beachside vs. Nampo old town), so 7–9 nights lets you split between neighborhoods.
alternatives: More Seoul: 10 / 4 / 8 (Gyeongju trimmed to a long weekend)

planningPrinciples: Use one practical hotel base per city; the only intentional return is the final two Seoul nights for a low-stress ICN departure.
Travel by direct KTX on city-change days, with only a light neighborhood plan after check-in.
Group sights by neighborhood rather than crisscrossing each city for a single attraction.
Keep a weather-friendly indoor alternative every day and avoid making time-sensitive events the sole anchor.
Treat all rail times, event dates, pricing, opening hours, and entry rules as details to verify in official apps and sites before purchase.

importantDates.label: CSAT / Suneung day
importantDates.note: Keep this Busan day deliberately low-stakes. The retained emergency research flags morning traffic management, later office/bank opening, and an approximately 13:05–13:40 aviation hold; verify the current notice before travel.

importantDates.label: 13:00 ICN departure
importantDates.note: Plan to be at the airport around three hours before an international departure, subject to airline guidance. Stay in Seoul the final two nights instead of attempting a same-day Busan-to-ICN connection.

trip.sourceNote: These are deliberately detailed planning blueprints synthesized from the retained transport, hotel, activity, food, savings, and emergency research. They are not confirmations or a live timetable.
trip.scheduleNote: Times below are intentional planning windows, not a live timetable. They are designed to make the day explicit while retaining enough buffer for weather, queues, rests, and transit.
trip.flightReconciliation: The Korea-based plan begins with a local ICN arrival at 21:00 on Nov. 1 and ends with a local ICN departure at 13:00 on Nov. 22. Because Seoul is well ahead of San Francisco, do not assume a Nov. 1 SFO departure can also be a Nov. 1 ICN arrival; reconcile the outbound calendar date, airline, terminal, and arrival time from the actual ticket before booking the first hotel night.
weatherAndPacking: Use layers rather than one heavy coat: a warm mid-layer, wind/rain shell, comfortable broken-in walking shoes, and evening accessories are more useful than a fixed temperature promise.
Check the actual forecast and AirKorea a few days before departure. The route includes outdoor palace, coast, park, and market days, but every one has an indoor or low-walking fallback.
Carry a compact umbrella or waterproof layer, a power bank, a universal Type C/F adapter, any personal medicines in original packaging, and a small day bag for train days.

budgetFrame.label: Stay strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Price live hotel rooms by exact dates and one-bed/private-bath requirements. The plans favor a practical Myeongdong/Seoul Station base, a station-oriented middle-city base, and one Haeundae base rather than costly hotel moves.

budgetFrame.label: Transport strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Direct KTX is the value/convenience default for city changes. T-money/WOWPASS-style local payment remains useful, but re-check current accepted cards, pass coverage, and actual fares.

budgetFrame.label: Experience strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Use a few paid anchors that matter to you, then layer in markets, parks, coastal walks, museums, and neighborhood food. Do not buy a pass solely because it is discounted; compare it with your actual saved list.

budgetFrame.label: Food strategy
budgetFrame.detail: Keep one quality meal or market experience per day, then use convenience-store, bakery, café, or hotel-neighborhood meals to protect pace and budget.

arrivalChecklist: Confirm hotel late check-in and save its Korean address before boarding the last flight.
Keep passport, arrival/entry confirmation, insurance contact, final hotel address, and an offline emergency card accessible before landing.
Choose the airport transfer based on live arrival time, luggage, terminal, and hotel—not a generic cheapest-fare rule.
Do not schedule sightseeing, a nonrefundable dinner, or a timed ticket on the arrival night.
departureChecklist: Complete online check-in and verify the airline terminal, baggage allowance, and airport cutoff the day before.
Pack passports, cards, devices, receipts/tax-refund paperwork, and medicines in a known carry-on location on Nov. 21.
Leave central Seoul early enough to be at ICN around three hours before the 13:00 international departure, following airline advice.
Handle airline, security, and any valid tax-refund process before duty-free browsing or a meal.
trip.budgetMethodNote: Hotel examples below multiply the retained research’s indicative one-room nightly USD ranges by the planned nights. They are planning math only: taxes, service fees, room type, weekend/date demand, currency conversion, promotions, and availability can materially change the real total.
dailySpendGuardrails: Keep food, local transit, and paid activities as separate envelopes rather than relying on the rough draft’s old all-in daily price. Your actual balance depends on how many paid anchors you keep.
Use the planner’s saved ideas and route days to identify the handful of paid tickets, reservations, spa/cooking-class choices, and special meals that deserve a confirmed budget.
Price the full transportation stack only after the airline, KTX trains, airport transfer, local payment card/pass, and hotel districts are selected.
flightBookingChecklist: Search to the actual local ICN arrival target first: 21:00 on Nov. 1. The originating SFO calendar date may be earlier because Seoul is far ahead of San Francisco.

Compare live direct and one-stop options by total arrival time, baggage/cancellation terms, seat comfort, airline terminal, and the ability to reach the Seoul hotel after immigration—not by an old fare screenshot.
After purchase, add flight numbers, both airport terminals, airline check-in cutoff, baggage allowance, seat assignment, and travel-insurance details to My plan.
Do not build a nonrefundable Seoul arrival-night plan until the flight and the hotel’s late check-in policy are confirmed.
